The way it works in the world of science is when a correlation between two variables is sufficient enough as substantiated by statistical formulas then the next step would be to design experiments to test this relationship. As one would expect, this is where you change the variable to see if it causes a change in another. These experiments are repeated to test for reliability. From there, other experiments are created to check for confounding variables (elements that may influence the results that were not accounted for). This process keeps going on until there is sufficient evidence to support a causal relationship between the two variables. If there is insufficient evidence then you go back to the drawing board to test for other variables that are responsible for the chance in the observed variable.
